stem: Which head circumference change is a red flag when monitoring a child with macrocephaly?

options.text: A head circumference that tracks along the 75th percentile
An increase in head circumference of more than 2 cm in a single month
A head circumference that is similar to the father's head circumference
Head circumference that plateaus after the first year of life
A head circumference that remains on a consistent percentile over time

explanation: An increase in head circumference of more than 2 cm in a single month is concerning because rapid head growth may indicate pathological accumulation of cerebrospinal fluid or blood.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because a consistently high percentile can be normal if the growth trajectory is steady.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because rapid head growth of this magnitude is a red flag for an underlying pathological process such as hydrocephalus or intracranial bleeding.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a family history of large head size supports benign familial macrocephaly.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because plateauing after an early rise is more consistent with a stable, benign pattern than a red flag for rapid expansion.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because staying on the same percentile suggests a stable growth pattern rather than accelerated head growth.

source.hint: Look for a specific rate of growth that suggests something other than standard tissue expansion.
